articles.title: AI Is Changing How Customers Choose Your Business
articles.author: Graham Kenny and Ganna Pogrebna
articles.summary: Drawing on three real SMB cases, a manufacturer, a boutique hotel, and a B2B software company, the authors show how AI is now sitting between your business and your buyers. Each company had to stop assuming customers came to them directly and start managing how AI tools described, recommended, or filtered them.
articles.whyItMatters: Your Google Business Profile is no longer your first impression. An AI summary might be. Read this to understand what you actually control now.

articles.title: 5 Marketing & Digital Trends: Week of July 20, 2026
articles.author: B2The7
articles.summary: Published this week, this tight briefing covers five concrete shifts landing right now: AI-generated images inside Google Overviews, ads appearing on nearly one in three commercial AI Mode queries, new ChatGPT Ads geo-exclusion controls, a new GA4 channel for tracking AI-referred traffic, and LinkedIn splitting reach into in-network and out-of-network. Each one comes with a clear so-what for small businesses running lean paid and organic programs.
articles.whyItMatters: GA4 now has a dedicated AI traffic channel. Set it up this week so you actually know how many visitors are arriving from ChatGPT and Perplexity, not just Google.

articles.title: This Week in Digital Marketing: Google's AI Business Summaries, TikTok Search Ads, and Tighter Email Rules
articles.author: Keene Digital
articles.summary: A practitioner-written roundup covering three specific changes that hit small businesses this week: Google testing AI-generated summaries on Business Profile listings built from your reviews, TikTok Search Ads opening to 14 local service categories including home services and dental, and tighter email spam thresholds dropping to 0.1% for bulk senders. Each item includes a direct action to take.
articles.whyItMatters: If your customers are under 40 and you offer a local service, TikTok Search Ads just opened a new placement your competitors probably haven't found yet.

articles.title: 15 AI Marketing Workflows for Small Business
articles.author: Teamday
articles.summary: Published July 15, this guide gives you 15 copy-ready AI marketing workflows built around customer outcomes, not tools. Each workflow has six defined parts: a trigger, input source, job, output, human review gate, and a measurement step. The core advice is to start with the workflow closest to lost revenue, not the most interesting one.
articles.whyItMatters: Pick one workflow, not fifteen. This guide tells you exactly how to build it so it actually runs week after week without falling apart.

articles.title: These Marketing Trends Are Helping Small Businesses Get Ahead in 2026
articles.author: Neil Patel
articles.summary: Neil Patel argues that the marketing funnel is broken and the real shift in 2026 is that AI doesn't just help with execution, it runs whole systems. Ranking in search matters less than being cited by AI. Small businesses that win aren't running more campaigns, they're designing better systems and hiring for judgment, not task execution.
articles.whyItMatters: If your brand only exists on your own website, you're invisible in more places than you think. This piece tells you what to fix first.

articles.title: AI for Small Businesses: 26 Essential Tools for Real Business Growth
articles.author: HubSpot
articles.summary: HubSpot's updated guide organizes 26 AI tools by business function, with honest notes on what each one actually solves, from 24/7 customer support gaps to lean-team content production. It includes real quotes from SMB operators and a clear framework for choosing tools based on your biggest current bottleneck, not what's trending.
articles.whyItMatters: You don't need 26 tools. But this list helps you figure out which two or three match the exact problem you're trying to solve right now.
